When on, your profile picture appears next to your name across the site.
Shows your live player at the top of your profile so people have one place to find your stream. Set up your stream.
When on, your name on posts you make links here, and hovering it shows a preview of your profile. Requires your profile to be public.
If you run a Dendritic Network node, put its payment address here and awards on your posts are paid straight to you over a payment channel — no transaction, so no gas fee for whoever is thanking you. Leave it blank and awards keep arriving as ordinary transfers, which is what most people want. Must start with https://.
Shows a Tip button next to your name on posts, articles, streams and your profile, so readers can send you something directly.
Tips are received through your existing payment channels. The pool does not hold your money; it aggregates eligible channels. Nothing is stored on this site — no balance, no list of who tipped you, no history. Your node works out what you have; this server only knows the switch is on.
Turning this on does not open a channel or move any funds. It needs a linked wallet and a payment-channel address above; without both, the Tip button stays hidden rather than failing when somebody clicks it.
What to call it — “Coffee fund”, “Beer money”. Defaults to “Tips”.
{# Who carries your tips, and on what terms (roadmap P15). The two modes are presented as a real choice with the safer one first and preselected, because they are genuinely different amounts of trust and a settings page that blurred them would be choosing on the user's behalf. #}
You do not need to run a node. A volunteer holds your incoming tips until you collect them, at the address in Payment-channel address above. Leave this blank and no Tip button appears — better than one that cannot deliver.
Where that volunteer keeps your incoming tips. This is not the same as your own payment-channel address above — one is your node, the other is theirs. Must start with https://.
How your tips are signed
The volunteer only carries messages. It holds no key of yours and cannot approve anything. Tips finish when you next open your wallet, so they can arrive while you are away but complete when you return.
You authorise the volunteer, on the blockchain, to approve incoming tips for you. It still cannot be paid, cannot take money out, and cannot close your channel — the contract refuses all three. You can withdraw the authorisation at any time and it stops immediately.
What you are trusting it with: a volunteer whose machine is compromised could take part in agreements about tips you have not collected yet. It can never touch your wallet.
Choosing this here records your preference; the authorisation itself is a transaction you sign with your own wallet below.
{# NO AUTHORISE BUTTON YET, deliberately. The browser flow that would send setDelegate to ChannelManagerV2 is not built. A button here would either do nothing or fake a success, and a control that appears to grant signing authority and does not is worse than no control at all — the creator would believe tips complete while they sleep, and they would not. The mode radio above still records a real preference, and it grants nothing on its own: authority comes from the contract, which has heard nothing until the transaction below is actually sent. #}
Delegated mode is not finished yet. Choosing it here records your preference but does not authorise anyone — that needs a blockchain transaction signed by your wallet, and the button for it is not built. Until then your tips are carried in mailbox mode, which needs no authorisation and is what the setting above defaults to.
Adds a live chat box to your profile page. Visitors join automatically with a random anonymous name; IP addresses are hidden.
Turns your profile background into a collaborative r/place-style pixel wall visitors can paint on: toggle paint mode, zoom in, and watch active painters live (their fresh pixels blink). A time-lapse scrubber along the bottom replays the most recent days. You can clear it anytime.
How many recent days of daily snapshots the time-lapse scrubber shows (1–60).
Log me out of my account after this many minutes of inactivity. 0 = stay logged in (default). Max 43200 (30 days).

The accent colours the Send button, your own name, and the online dots.
Custom HTML tags like <div>, <table>, <marquee> are allowed. Scripts are stripped.
Placing your stream & chat: put <div id="stream-slot"></div> or <div id="chat-slot"></div> anywhere in your HTML, and your stream player / chat box moves into that spot and fills it (style the slot with CSS to control size). Without a slot they stay at the top / bottom as before.

Username & password
